From c06344939422bbd032ac967223a7863de57496b5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eric Whitney <enwlinux@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Mar 2014 23:34:16 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] ext4: fix partial cluster handling for bigalloc file systems

Commit 9cb00419fa, which enables hole punching for bigalloc file
systems, exposed a bug introduced by commit 6ae06ff51e in an earlier
release.  When run on a bigalloc file system, xfstests generic/013, 068,
075, 083, 091, 100, 112, 127, 263, 269, and 270 fail with e2fsck errors
or cause kernel error messages indicating that previously freed blocks
are being freed again.

The latter commit optimizes the selection of the starting extent in
ext4_ext_rm_leaf() when hole punching by beginning with the extent
supplied in the path argument rather than with the last extent in the
leaf node (as is still done when truncating).  However, the code in
rm_leaf that initially sets partial_cluster to track cluster sharing on
extent boundaries is only guaranteed to run if rm_leaf starts with the
last node in the leaf.  Consequently, partial_cluster is not correctly
initialized when hole punching, and a cluster on the boundary of a
punched region that should be retained may instead be deallocated.

Signed-off-by: Eric Whitney <enwlinux@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: "Theodore Ts'o" <tytso@mit.edu>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org

diff --git a/fs/ext4/extents.c b/fs/ext4/extents.c
index 17b2fb2e8d19..e35f93b4cb13 100644
--- a/fs/ext4/extents.c
+++ b/fs/ext4/extents.c
@@ -2597,6 +2597,27 @@ ext4_ext_rm_leaf(handle_t *handle, struct inode *inode,
 	ex_ee_block = le32_to_cpu(ex->ee_block);
 	ex_ee_len = ext4_ext_get_actual_len(ex);
 
+	/*
+	 * If we're starting with an extent other than the last one in the
+	 * node, we need to see if it shares a cluster with the extent to
+	 * the right (towards the end of the file). If its leftmost cluster
+	 * is this extent's rightmost cluster and it is not cluster aligned,
+	 * we'll mark it as a partial that is not to be deallocated.
+	 */
+
+	if (ex != EXT_LAST_EXTENT(eh)) {
+		ext4_fsblk_t current_pblk, right_pblk;
+		long long current_cluster, right_cluster;
+
+		current_pblk = ext4_ext_pblock(ex) + ex_ee_len - 1;
+		current_cluster = (long long)EXT4_B2C(sbi, current_pblk);
+		right_pblk = ext4_ext_pblock(ex + 1);
+		right_cluster = (long long)EXT4_B2C(sbi, right_pblk);
+		if (current_cluster == right_cluster &&
+			EXT4_PBLK_COFF(sbi, right_pblk))
+			*partial_cluster = -right_cluster;
+	}
+
 	trace_ext4_ext_rm_leaf(inode, start, ex, *partial_cluster);
 
 	while (ex >= EXT_FIRST_EXTENT(eh) &&
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `fs/ext4/extents.c`**
- Added a new block of code in the `ext4_ext_rm_leaf` function to handle the case when the starting extent is not the last one in the node. 
- This new code checks if the current extent shares a cluster with the next extent and if it is not cluster-aligned. If both conditions are met, it marks the current extent as a partial cluster that should not be deallocated by setting `*partial_cluster` to `-right_cluster`.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modification in `ext4_ext_rm_leaf` addresses a bug related to partial cluster handling when hole punching in bigalloc file systems. The newly added logic ensures that when the starting extent is not the last one, the code correctly identifies and retains any clusters that should not be deallocated, thus preventing potential data loss and errors that were previously introduced by an earlier commit. This change is crucial for maintaining the integrity of the file system during operations that involve modifying extents.
